title: Testing and Software Development Lifecycle
concept:
Testing must be embedded in the chosen Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) — it is not an afterthought. Each SDLC handles testing differently.

**Sequential lifecycles (waterfall, V-model)** define phases performed in order: requirements → design → implementation → testing → maintenance. The **V-model** explicitly pairs each development phase with a corresponding test level: requirements ↔ acceptance testing, system design ↔ system testing, architectural design ↔ integration testing, detailed design ↔ component testing. The V-model emphasises that test design should begin as soon as the corresponding development artifact is available — even though execution happens later.

**Iterative and incremental lifecycles (RUP, spiral, prototyping)** break the work into phases that are repeated. Each iteration produces a slice of working software which is tested before the next iteration begins. Risk-driven iteration (spiral) prioritises tackling the highest-risk areas first.

**Agile lifecycles (Scrum, XP, Kanban)** produce working software every sprint or continuously. Testing happens throughout each sprint: test planning at sprint planning, test design alongside development, execution before the sprint ends, regression and acceptance test automation continuously.

The key principle: every SDLC includes all the testing activities, but with different timing, granularity, and formality.
keyPoints: Sequential lifecycles separate phases; the V-model maps each dev phase to a corresponding test level.
Iterative and incremental lifecycles repeat phases on shorter cycles, testing each increment.
Agile teams perform all test activities continuously, with heavy automation to keep up with each sprint.

quiz.question: In the V-model, which test level is MOST closely paired with the requirements specification?
quiz.explanation: Acceptance testing verifies that the system meets the original business requirements and user needs — the V-model pairs it with the requirements phase. System testing is paired with system design, integration with architectural design, and component testing with detailed design.
